paper.title: Loneliness, Hopelessness, and Meaning in Life among Young Adults Following a Romantic Breakup
paper.journal: International Journal of Marketing & Human Resource Research

claims.text: Loneliness is negatively associated with meaning in life among young adults following a romantic breakup.
claims.evidence: The results showed that loneliness was negatively associated with meaning in life

claims.text: Loneliness does not make a significant unique contribution to meaning in life when hopelessness is included in the regression model.
claims.evidence: loneliness was negatively associated with meaning in life, although it did not make a significant unique contribution when hopelessness was included in the regression model

claims.text: Hopelessness emerged as a significant negative predictor and the strongest variable in predicting meaning in life after romantic breakup.
claims.evidence: Hopelessness, in contrast, emerged as a significant negative predictor and the strongest variable in the model

claims.text: Loneliness and hopelessness together explained 49.2% of the variance in meaning in life among young adults after romantic breakup.
claims.evidence: Together, loneliness and hopelessness explained 49.2% of the variance in meaning in life

claims.text: Hopelessness is more strongly related to the Presence of Meaning than to the Search for Meaning dimension among young adults following romantic breakup.
claims.evidence: Additional findings indicated that hopelessness was more strongly related to the Presence of Meaning than to the Search for Meaning

claims.text: Meaning in life after a romantic breakup is more closely associated with hope, future orientation, and confidence in the possibility of a better life than with loneliness alone.
claims.evidence: meaning in life after a romantic breakup is more closely associated with hope, future orientation, and confidence in the possibility of a better life than with loneliness alone

claims.text: A romantic breakup may represent both an emotional and an existential experience that challenges young adults' ability to preserve or reconstruct meaning in life.
claims.evidence: a romantic breakup may represent both an emotional and an existential experience that challenges young adults' ability to preserve or reconstruct meaning in life

claims.text: Loneliness represents the relational and emotional dimension of post-breakup adjustment, whereas hopelessness reflects the cognitive and future-oriented dimension.
claims.evidence: loneliness represents the relational and emotional dimension of post-breakup adjustment, whereas hopelessness reflects the cognitive and future-oriented dimension
